policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'the things whereof ye wrote' renders no dative object; the +μοι reading would give 'ye wrote unto me'.
ASV 'render unto the wife her due' renders the single noun ὀφειλήν; ὀφειλομένην εὔνοιαν would give 'due benevolence/goodwill'.
Aorist vs present subjunctive of the same verb; ASV 'that ye may give yourselves unto prayer' expresses no aspectual difference.
ASV names prayer only; the RP reading adds νηστείᾳ καί, which the ASV would render 'fasting and prayer'.
ASV 'may be together again' renders the copula ἦτε with ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό; συνέρχησθε is rendered 'come together' elsewhere in the ASV.
ASV text 'Yet I would' renders δέ, and the mapped textual note 'Many ancient authorities read For' assigns γάρ to the margin.
Word order only; 'each man hath his own gift' fixes no Greek order.
ὁ μέν and ὃς μέν are both rendered 'one after this manner'; the English does not distinguish article from relative here.
ὁ δέ and ὃς δέ are both rendered 'another after that'; the English does not distinguish them.
Presence or absence of the copula ἐστιν; English must supply 'is' in 'It is good for them' either way.
Aorist vs present infinitive of γαμέω; ASV 'to marry' renders either.
Word order of λέγω ἐγώ only; ASV 'say I' does not fix the Greek order.

ASV 'And the woman that hath an unbelieving husband' is a relative clause (ἥτις), against the conditional 'if any woman hath' that εἴ τις would give, and unlike v.12 where the ASV does write 'If any brother hath'.
οὗτος and αὐτός are both carried by the ASV's 'he is content to dwell with her'.
ASV 'let her not leave her husband' renders the noun τὸν ἄνδρα, not the pronoun αὐτόν.
ASV 'is sanctified in the brother' renders ἀδελφῷ; ἀνδρί would give 'in the husband'.
ASV text 'God hath called us' renders ἡμᾶς, and the mapped textual note 'Many ancient authorities read you' puts ὑμᾶς in the margin.
Aorist vs perfect of μερίζω; the ASV's 'hath distributed' renders either tense in this idiom.
ASV 'as the Lord hath distributed to each man' has κύριος as the subject of the distributing.
ASV 'as God hath called each' has θεός as the subject of the calling, the reverse of the RP pairing.
ASV marks the two clauses differently: 'Was any man called being circumcised?' (aorist) against 'Hath any been called in uncircumcision?', whose English perfect renders κέκληται.
ASV 'likewise he that was called being free' renders ὁμοίως alone, with no 'also' for the added καί.
Two aorist forms of the same verb; ASV 'shouldest thou marry' renders either.

ASV takes τὸ λοιπόν with the ἵνα clause ('that henceforth both those that have wives'), which the RP order τὸ λοιπὸν ἐστίν excludes; the remaining pair differs only in punctuation, which the English cannot settle. The note here is an alternative_rendering and does not decide a reading.
ASV 'those that use the world' has no demonstrative; τῷ κόσμῳ τούτῳ would give 'this world' in that clause, as the ASV does write later for the fashion of this world.
Subjunctive vs future after πῶς; ASV 'how he may please the Lord' renders either.
Subjunctive vs future after πῶς; ASV 'how he may please his wife' renders either. The verse note concerns the v.34 clause division, not this form.
ASV 'So also the woman that is unmarried' renders the καί the RP text omits, and the mapped textual note assigns the RP arrangement to the margin.

ASV 'the woman that is unmarried and the virgin is careful for the things of the Lord' keeps ἡ ἄγαμος with ἡ γυνή, the reading the mapped note contrasts with 'the wife and the virgin. She that is unmarried is careful'.
ASV has no fresh sentence 'She that is unmarried is careful' after 'the virgin'; that added Ἡ ἄγαμος appears only in the mapped textual note as another authorities' reading.
Article with σώματι; ASV 'in body' shows no article either way.
Article with πνεύματι; ASV 'in spirit' shows no article either way.
Subjunctive vs future after πῶς; ASV 'how she may please her husband' renders either.
σύμφορον and συμφέρον are alike rendered 'profit'; the ASV note here is an alternative_rendering about 'snare' and does not touch this unit.
Two compounds of the same sense; ASV 'attend upon the Lord' renders either.
ASV 'standeth stedfast in his heart' renders the possessive αὐτοῦ, which the RP phrase ἑδραῖος ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ lacks.
ASV 'hath determined this in his own heart' renders ἰδίᾳ 'own'; καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ would give plain 'his heart', as in the earlier clause.
Bare infinitive vs articular τοῦ τηρεῖν; ASV 'to keep' renders either.
ASV 'shall do well' is future, rendering ποιήσει rather than the present ποιεῖ.
γαμίζων and ἐκγαμίζων are alike rendered 'he that giveth ... in marriage'.

ASV 'his own virgin daughter' renders the phrase, so the RP omission is excluded; the two surviving readings differ only in the order of ἑαυτοῦ, which the English does not fix. The verse note is an alternative_rendering about 'daughter'.
ASV's correlative 'both he that giveth ... and he that giveth her not' renders καὶ ... καὶ; ὁ δέ would give an adversative 'but he that'.
γαμίζων and ἑκγαμίζων are alike rendered 'he that giveth her not in marriage'.
ASV 'shall do better' is future, rendering ποιήσει rather than the present ποιεῖ.
ASV 'A wife is bound for so long time as her husband liveth' has no 'by the law' for the added νόμῳ.
ASV 'but if the husband be dead' renders δέ alone, with no 'also' for the added καί.
ASV renders no causal particle in v.40 ('But she is happier ... and I think'); γάρ would give 'for'.
